summary: This is a research proposal by Dr. Ashish Rajput (VitaLabs) for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) rejuvenation using single-cell RNA-seq data analysis and AI/ML-assisted gene regulatory network modeling to identify aging-disrupted pathways. The project has completed a computational discovery phase identifying lead candidate genes and now proposes in vitro, organoid, and in vivo validation using young and aged human primary HSCs, alongside drug discovery efforts. The current TRL is approximately 1–2, as the work is transitioning from computational target identification to experimental validation.

content_blocks.title: Project Title and Principal Investigator
content_blocks.content: Title: 'Hematopoietic Stem Cell Rejuvenation using combined modulation of aging-disrupted pathways identified by human single-cell data analysis'. Principal Investigator: Dr. Ashish Rajput, PhD. Funded by VitaLabs.

content_blocks.title: Disease Background and Clinical Rationale
content_blocks.content: HSCs generate all blood and immune cells throughout life. With aging, HSCs undergo functional decline resulting in: impaired blood cell production, reduced regenerative capacity, increased susceptibility to infections, anemia, and hematologic malignancies (myelodysplastic syndromes, leukemia). Aged HSCs display myeloid-biased differentiation, contributing to chronic inflammation and impaired adaptive immunity — key drivers of age-related frailty. Restoring youthful HSC function has clinical implications for healthy aging and prevention of age-associated hematologic and immune disorders.

content_blocks.title: Molecular Mechanisms of HSC Aging
content_blocks.content: Intrinsic mechanisms: DNA damage accumulation, telomere shortening, mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic drift — leading to altered transcriptional programs, reduced self-renewal, and skewed differentiation. Extrinsic mechanisms: aging bone marrow niche contributes via inflammatory cytokines, impaired stromal support, and altered signaling pathways (Wnt, Notch, TGF-β, mTOR). Together these reduce regenerative potential and compromise hematopoietic homeostasis.

content_blocks.title: Limitations of Current Therapeutic Strategies
content_blocks.content: Bone marrow transplantation: can rejuvenate hematopoiesis but carries risks of graft-versus-host disease, donor compatibility issues, and is not feasible as a broad anti-aging strategy. Pharmacological interventions (rapamycin, NAD+ boosters): systemic effects, lack specificity for HSCs. Senolytics and anti-inflammatory agents: may indirectly improve the niche but do not directly address molecular dysfunction within HSCs. Conclusion: need for precise, stem-cell–focused strategies.

content_blocks.title: Technology Platform — scRNA-seq and AI/ML GRN Analysis
content_blocks.content: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables cell-type–specific molecular profiling of rare HSC populations, capturing aging-specific transcriptional changes that bulk sequencing masks. Combined with multi-omics integration and gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis, scRNA-seq provides a framework to identify and prioritize molecular drivers of HSC dysfunction. The team uses AI/ML-assisted GRN modeling including the AubrAI terminal tool.

content_blocks.title: Completed Work — Computational Discovery Phase
content_blocks.content: In a VitaLabs-funded project, the team systematically analyzed publicly available and proprietary human scRNA-seq datasets spanning different ages and genders. Using enhanced computational pipelines developed over the past decade and applied in high-impact publications, they mapped aging-specific molecular signatures of HSCs and their niches. Through scRNA-seq data analysis and AI/ML-assisted GRN modeling (including AubrAI terminal), they identified and prioritized several lead candidate genes whose dysregulation drives HSC decline. These represent promising intervention points for rejuvenation. NOTE: No quantitative experimental results, specific gene names, or statistical data are disclosed in this document.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Work — Experimental Validation and Drug Discovery
content_blocks.content: Planned activities: (1) In vitro validation using young and aged human primary HSCs. (2) Organoid and in vivo model validation through CRO or academic partnerships. (3) Interventional modalities depending on gene expression direction: mRNA overexpression via electroporation, siRNA knockdown, or CRISPR-based activation/inhibition. (4) Drug discovery: computational chemistry, QSAR-based docking, and potential gene therapy approaches to restore youthful HSC function. No timelines, specific CRO names, or quantitative targets are specified.
